summary: INITIAL AUDIT baseline (no app code changed). Wrote one small isolated harness and test file: 26 cases, 17 passed and 9 strict-xfail (each xfail is a fault that was reproduced). Ran 3 times with the same result, no flaky cases. Every tejas/server Motor handle was rebound to the tejas_isolated_iter134 DB, and the test asserts that no real handle is left. The DB was dropped afterward and its absence verified. MONGO_URL/DB_NAME were not changed, no lifespan or AI worker ran, there was no real login, and grade dispatch from submit was swapped for a no-op recorder. Confirmed faults: (1) An app clock running ahead seals valid attempts early through answer, visit, bonus, read (expire) and history. (2) finalize() trusts the reason passed in by the caller. (3) render_crop for PDFs skips the source SHA check. (4) The phone and login limiters return 500 on a first-upsert DuplicateKeyError. (5) unpack decodes the JSON again on every call and does not merge concurrent cold reads (32x amplification measured). Ruled out: owned() checks the user before hydrate, and the browser's 5s recover only flushes dirty drafts. The canonical answer invariants held: 25 replays produced exactly one revision, a changed body got 409, a stale new request got 409, a late write got 409, a foreign user got 404, and the save-vs-seal race stayed consistent.

critical.endpoint: PUT /api/attempts/{id}/answers/{qid}, POST /visit, POST /bonus, GET /attempts/{id} (expire), GET /attempts (history); also expire() callers results/asset/retry/report/start
critical.issue: CONFIRMED premature seal: the precheck `now() >= deadline` uses the app clock and, when true, calls finalize(id,'time_limit'). With the app clock 3600s ahead and a real DB deadline 600s in the future, all 5 routes sealed the attempt: status=completed, reason=time_limit, submitted_at 600s before the deadline. The valid answer, visit and bonus commands were rejected with 409 'The attempt has ended'. Read and history returned 200 but had already sealed it. Repro: test_app_clock_ahead_does_not_seal_valid_attempt[answer|visit|bonus|read_expire|history].

CONFIRMED: finalize() itself uses $$NOW correctly. Direct calls with the app clock skewed gave reason=submitted for a future deadline and time_limit with submitted_at=deadline for an expired one. But when the deadline has not passed, the caller's reason is stored as-is: finalize(id,'time_limit') on a future deadline stores reason=time_limit, sealed 600s early. This is how the app-clock prechecks turn into wrong seals. Fix: use the reason only if the DB says the deadline has passed, or on explicit submit; otherwise do not seal at all for time_limit. Repro: test_finalize_time_limit_reason_requires_db_expiry.

CONFIRMED: when the source is a PDF, its bytes are never compared with source.sha256. In the test, get_object returned tampered bytes and crop_png was still called once on them (sha 91f3e1... instead of the declared b6833d...). No error was raised and a PNG came back. The rendered_png path does raise ValueError (baseline test passes). The cache identity also uses the declared sha, so a crop made from tampered bytes is cached under the trusted key. Repro: test_render_crop_pdf_rejects_sha_mismatch (mocked get_object and crop_png, no real PDF).

CONFIRMED (deterministic fake): the limiter find_one_and_update(upsert=True) has no DuplicateKeyError handling or retry. Injecting a single DuplicateKeyError gives HTTP 500 on both routes. On real isolated Mongo 7.0, 32 concurrent first upserts on the same _id produced 0 DuplicateKeyErrors (the server retries internally) with a correct final count of 32. So the race is hidden on this topology, but the code path still returns 500 if it happens (other versions/sharding, driver retry edge cases). Fix: catch the error and retry once. Repro: test_limiter_first_upsert_duplicate_key_handled[phone|login].

minor.issue: Baseline on real isolated Mongo, not a fake. 100-question pack, raw size 123,083 B. 32 concurrent cold reads made 32 find_one calls, 32 zlib decompress calls, 32 SHA checks and 32 json.loads calls (no single-flight, x32 amplification) in about 43ms. 32 warm reads made 0 DB reads but still 32 json.loads (about 0.21ms per decode, about 9ms total). The cache holds raw bytes only (32MiB byte bound), so every hit decodes again. Mutation isolation is OK: each caller gets a fresh object. This is a local micro-baseline and does NOT qualify 500k.

With the app clock 3600s behind and the DB deadline passed, answer and visit are correctly rejected (409, no answer stored) by the $$NOW guard. But GET /attempts/{id} reports status 'active' past the deadline and does not seal. The attempt stays open until a DB-clock path runs; finalize later records submitted_at=deadline, so the score is not affected.
Code review: falls back to get(attempts,id), which hydrates the full pack on every save. Ownership was already checked by the prior user-scoped find_one, but this is costly for legacy rows.

ruled_out: owned() checks ownership before hydrate: GET read, results, asset, PUT answer, visit and submit by a foreign synthetic user all returned 404 with 0 hydrate calls. The query includes user_id. The audit-doc phrase 'ownership after hydration' does not apply to owned() or these routes.

Browser 5s recover (useAttempt.js:187-215) calls load() only if data.current is null, then flush(), which loops over the dirty drafts only. There is no full poll once loaded. Caveat: confirmDeadline does a full GET /attempts/{id} every 5-6.5s, but only after the countdown reaches 0. That means a deadline herd for synchronized exams.

baseline_canonical_invariants_real_isola.replay_25_same_command: 25/25 got 200, exactly 1 applied (24 duplicate), server_seq=1, command_count=1, 1 receipt, revision=1
baseline_canonical_invariants_real_isola.late_write_after_submit: 409 and not stored; replaying the old command after the seal returns 200 duplicate=true; sealed_seq=server_seq=1
baseline_canonical_invariants_real_isola.save_vs_seal_race: 5 interleave delays. Seen splits: 2 acked/18 got 409, 16/4, 20/0. In all cases acked == stored == sealed_seq and no acked seq is greater than sealed_seq.

action_items: Remove the app-clock deadline prechecks that call finalize in answers.save_answer, visit_question, unlock_bonus, expire() and history. Either rely on the $$NOW-guarded CAS only, or have finalize do a conditional seal for time_limit only when the DB says the deadline has passed ($expr deadline<=$$NOW), without sealing otherwise. Return a 409 based on the DB result.
finalize: do not store a caller-supplied 'time_limit' reason (or seal) when the DB deadline is still in the future.
render_crop: for PDF sources, check sha256(get_object(path)) == source['sha256'] before crop_png, and fail closed (as the PNG path does). Include the sha of the verified bytes in the cache identity.
Catch DuplicateKeyError and retry once in the phone.py and auth.login limiter upsert.
packs: add single-flight for cold unpack, and consider caching the decoded immutable structure (deep-copied or frozen per caller) to avoid decoding on every hit. Keep authorization out of the cache.

After the fixes, remove the strict xfail markers (they will XPASS and fail strict) and rerun: cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest test_iter134_canonical_faults_isolated.py -n0 -p no:cacheprovider -v
critical_code_review_comments: attempts.py is 658 lines and close to the 700-line split guideline.
Deadline semantics are split: CAS guards use $$NOW, while prechecks and expire use the app clock. There should be a single canonical time source.
derivatives cache key trusts declared metadata rather than verified bytes.
Frontend confirmDeadline at 0s triggers a full hydrated GET for every synchronized student. Consider a light status endpoint or projection later (not a polling bug).

success_rate.backend: 17/17 invariant/baseline cases pass; 9/9 targeted fault reproductions confirmed (strict xfail)

test_credentials: None used. Synthetic ephemeral actors TEST_U134_student/other exist only in the isolated DB. The login fault test used a nonexistent example.com email with a dummy string, and the DuplicateKeyError fires before any credential check.
seed_data_creation: Only in tejas_isolated_iter134 (TEST_ prefixed attempts and packs), which was dropped after each run; absence verified via mongosh.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use iso_harness_iter134 (OFFSET-able app clock; Mongo $$NOW real). API responses are enveloped as {data,error,meta}; use the J() helper. Do NOT run legacy test_v5_faults.py or test_ai_tags_review.py. Run with -n0 (pytest.ini forces xdist). Submit's ensure_grade is patched to a no-op in this file. Mongo 7.0.45 standalone.
rca of the issue: Premature seal: answers.py:70, attempts.py:87/305/333/362 compare the app time.time() with the deadline. If that is true, they call finalize(id,'time_limit'). finalize's filter only checks status=active, and its $cond keeps the caller's reason when the deadline has not expired. So any app/DB clock skew (or a skewed worker among many) seals active exams early and refuses valid saves. Mitigation: make the DB clock the only authority for time_limit sealing.
